svg.title: Twelve questions — what must be checked next?
svg.desc: The project separates mathematical, textual, and applied verification. This is not a historical teacher–student chart.

g.font-family: Noto Sans CJK JP, Noto Sans JP, sans-serif
g.text: Twelve questions — what must be checked next?
The project separates mathematical, textual, and applied verification.
01 Notation and translation / 02 Elimination and determinants
Match every source symbol to an edition and page.
A and B are proved and tested; authorial intent remains a separate question.
03 Fixed products / 04 Pi and enri
Check meanings and generation rules separately; do not label everything “lost.”
Distinguish a modern approximation from the quantity actually extrapolated historically.
05 Mensuration / 06 Higher-degree equations
Compare validity conditions; never publish an unsourced chain of names.
Separate numerical roots, elimination, and radicals; do not claim a solution of all higher degrees.
07 Six-sphere chain / 08 Surveying and calendars
Separate the 1822 dedication, 1832 record, and 1936 Soddy paper; test closure separately.
Distinguish Ishiguro’s teachers by subject; co-appearance does not prove direct instruction.
09 Primary materials / 10 Variants and editions
Record holdings, images, and pages read; “not collected” is not “nonexistent.”
Separate transcription, missing numbers, reordered tables, and reversed representatives.
11 Attribution / 12 Modern applications
Separate source, prior scholarship, modern reconstruction, and unverified claims.
Separate models from tested devices; listed device applications remain untested.
The article explains all twelve items. This is not a historical teacher–student chart.
AI NOBORU | Updated 15 September 2026 | Sources and variants appear in the article
